{{Short description|Italian theoretical biologist}}
{{For|the Italian Olympic gymnast|Marcello Barbieri (gymnast)}}
{{Autobiography|date=February 2016}}

[[File:Marcello Barbieri.jpg|thumb]]
'''Marcello Barbieri''' (born 1940) is an Italian [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|theoretical biologist]] at the [[University of Ferrara]] whose main interest is the origin of novelties in [[macroevolution]]. He has been one of founders and first editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Biosemiotics (journal)|Biosemiotics]]'' until 2012; currently, he is an editor of the journal ''[[BioSystems]]''. His research field is code biology, the study of all codes of life from the [[genetic code]] to the codes of culture. His major books are ''The Semantic Theory of Evolution'' (1985),<ref name="uno">Barbieri M (1985) The Semantic Theory of Evolution. ''Harwood Academic Publishers'', New York</ref> ''The Organic Codes'' (2003),<ref name="due">Barbieri M (2003) The Organic Codes. ''Cambridge University Press'', Cambridge, UK</ref> and ''Code Biology. A New Science of Life'' (2015).<ref name="tre">Barbieri M (2015) Code Biology. A New Science of Life. ''Springer'', Dordrecht</ref>

==Career==
Barbieri graduated in 1964 from the Science Faculty of [[University of Bologna|Bologna University]].<ref name="Favareau">Favareau D (ed) (2010). ''Essential Readings in Biosemiotics: Anthology and Commentary''. Springer, Dordrecht, p. 751-755. ''Comments on Barbieri's work pp. 58-62''</ref> In 1965, he was employed by the [[Medical school|Medical Faculty]] of the same University as a researcher in [[molecular biology]] and teacher of [[biophysics]] for medical students. He conducted research at the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] in Cambridge, the [[National Institutes of Health]] in Bethesda, and the [[Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics]] in Berlin. Since 1992 he is professor of [[embryology]] at the Medical Faculty of [[University of Ferrara|Ferrara University]]. In 1997, he founded the Italian Association for Theoretical Biology<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.ingentaconnect.com/content/imp/chk/2001/00000008/00000003/91|title=Living forms are communicative structures, based on the organic codes|last=Kull|first=K.|journal=Cybernetics & Human Knowing|volume=8|issue=3|date=March 1, 2001|pages=91–94|publisher=Imprint Academic}}</ref> (Associazione Italiana di Biologia Teorica) and in 2012 he founded the International Society of Code Biology.<ref name="Callebaut">{{cite journal | last1 = Barbieri | first1 = M | year = 2014 | title = From Biosemiotics to Code Biology | journal = Biological Theory | volume = 9 | issue = 2| pages = 239–249 | doi=10.1007/s13752-013-0155-6| s2cid = 84746904 }}</ref>

==Research==
At the Max-Planck-Institut in Berlin, Barbieri obtained the largest microcrystals of eukaryotic [[ribosome]]s that have ever appeared in the scientific literature.<ref name="Journal">{{cite journal | last1 = Barbieri | first1 = M | year = 1979 | title = Ribosome crystallization in homogenates and cell extracts of chick embryos | url = http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/107628079/abstract?CRETRY=1&SRETRY=0 | journal = Journal of Supramolecular Structure | volume = 10 | issue = 3| pages = 349–357 | doi=10.1002/jss.400100306| pmid = 573827 | url-access = subscription }}{{dead link|date=February 2019|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> At the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] in Cambridge, and at the [[National Institutes of Health]] in Bethesda, he developed mathematical models for the reconstruction of structures from incomplete information and has shown that a convergent increase in complexity is possible if the reconstructions are performed with iterative methods that make use of memories and codes.<ref name="sei">{{cite journal | last1 = Barbieri | first1 = M | year = 2016 | title = A new theory of development: the generation of complexity in ontogenesis | doi = 10.1098/rsta.2015.0148 | pmid = 26857661 | bibcode = 2016RSPTA.37450148B | journal = Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A | volume = 374 | issue = 2063| article-number = 20150148 | doi-access = free }}</ref> He has proposed that the existence of organic codes is revealed by the presence of adaptors and has shown that such codes exist in signal transduction, in the [[cytoskeleton]] and in cell compartments.<ref name="due" /> This adaptor-dependent definition of code has been used by Kühn and Hofmeyr<ref name="Kuhn">{{cite journal | last1 = Kühn | first1 = S | last2 = Hofmeyr J-H | first2 = S | year = 2014 | title = Is the "Histone Code" an organic code? | journal = Biosemiotics | volume = 7 | issue = 2| pages = 203–222 | doi=10.1007/s12304-014-9211-2| s2cid = 14123516 }}</ref> to show that the [[histone code]] is a true organic code, whereas Gérard Battail has argued that "Barbieri's organic codes enable error correction of genomes".<ref name="Battail">{{cite journal | last1 = Battail | first1 = Gérard | year = 2014 | title = Barbieri's Organic Codes Enable Error Correction of Genomes | journal = Biosemiotics | volume = 7 | issue = 2| pages = 259–277 | doi=10.1007/s12304-014-9216-x| s2cid = 11070602 }}</ref> He has been described as one of 'key figures' in [[biosemiotics]] by Donald Favareau in Essential Readings,<ref name="Favareau" /> by Liz Else in New Scientist<ref>{{cite journal|journal=New Scientist|date=August 21, 2010|volume=207|issue=2774|pages=28–31|doi=10.1016/S0262-4079(10)62035-0|bibcode=2010NewSc.207Q..28E|title=A meadowful of meaning|first=Liz|last=Else|quote=Marcello Barbieri, a molecular biologist at the University of Ferrara in Italy, another key figure, echoes Favareau. He brings yet another perspective to the field – a "code model" that he has applied to the genetic code, splicing and other cellular codes.}}</ref> and by Nigel Williams in ''Current Biology''.<ref name=signs>{{cite journal|journal=Current Biology|date=September 4, 2007|volume=17|issue=17|page=R735–R737|doi=10.1016/j.cub.2007.08.025|title=Signs of the times|first=Nigel|last=Williams|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Theoretical work==
Barbieri underlined that copying and coding are two fundamentally different mechanisms of molecular change and suggested that there are two distinct mechanisms of evolutionary change: evolution by natural selection, based on copying, and evolution by natural conventions, based on coding. This in turn implies that many organic codes appeared in the history of life after the genetic code, and Barbieri proposed that the greatest novelties of [[macroevolution]] were associated with the origin of new codes. These ideas have been developed in the course of a thirty-year period in the books: ''The Semantic Theory of Evolution'' (1985),<ref name="uno" /> ''The Organic Codes'' (2003)<ref name="due" /> and ''Code Biology'' (2015).<ref name="tre" />
